predecessors.name: Tibetans (Era of Fragmentation)
predecessors.text: the Tibetan lands of Cliopatria's Tibetans row (to 1259); the Mongols invaded Tibet in 1240 and 1244 and Sakya Pandita gained power over Tibet through the Mongols in 1244

predecessors.name: Mongol Empire
predecessors.text: Ü-Tsang, as the Tibet dossier (ea-06-b) draws it: the gazetteer's Central Tibet without Chamdo (Kham) and without the Guge, Latö and Mangyül Gungthang circles of West Tibet.

successors.name: Tibet
successors.text: Ü-Tsang, as the Tibet dossier (ea-06-b) draws it: the gazetteer's Central Tibet without Chamdo (Kham) and without the Guge, Latö and Mangyül Gungthang circles of West Tibet.

ledger.x: 1264: Kublai Khan gives Phagpa the rule of Tibet.

c. 1265: Mangyül Gungthang is founded under Sakya overlordship. The infobox of its page: Tibetan kingdom under Sakya overlordship, one of the thirteen myriarchies, ruled by a Sakya lama viceroy appointed by the Yuan court; Established c. 1265. Drawn as a vassal tint until the Sakya regime ends.
1285: the Drikung Kagyu rise against the Sakya.
1354: Changchub Gyaltsen's Phagmodrupa begin to supersede the Sakya.
1358 (bridging): the Sakya overlordship over Mangyül Gungthang ends with the Sakya regime.
1358: central Tibet passes to the Phagmodrupa.

wars.name: Drikung revolt
wars.outcome: The Yuan army under Temür Buqa and the Sakyas suppress the Drikung Kagyu revolt in 1290: Drigung Monastery is burned and about 10,000 are killed.

wars.name: Mongol campaigns in Tibet
wars.outcome: A 1268 expedition under Manggudai and a 1275 campaign by Aurughchi; by 1280 Mongol rule was considered secure.

wars.name: Phagmodrupa supersession of the Sakya
wars.outcome: Changchub Gyaltsen's Phagmodrupa take central Tibet from the Sakya; the Sakya lamas' rule ends in 1358 and the Yuan, beset by the Red Turbans, confirms the new lord's gains.

certainty.note: Tibetan lordships without surveyed frontiers; the Yuan Routes of Kham and Amdo and the western marches are outside the shape.
